items.text: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] at line 503 will raise a KeyError for pre-existing integrations that lack the sender key in their metadata, since build_integration only adds sender conditionally and other code paths already guard against this

OAuth authorize redirect URL is assembled via string interpolation; if redirect_uri or other params contain characters needing escaping, this can produce a malformed URL or unintended query parsing; should use a proper query encoder
The predictable OAuth state allows an attacker to send a forged setup callback that binds the attacker's GitHub login and installation_id into a victim's pipeline, defeating the user-match check

safe_urlopen() and get_user_info() can raise network errors or non-2xx via raise_for_status(), which would 500 the install flow; should catch those exceptions and return the error() page to keep failures user-safe

test_installation_not_found now passes for the wrong reason: it sends a state that doesn't match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView rejects at the state check before build_integration runs; the 404 stub is never hit and the 'installation could not be found' path is untested

integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] assumes the nested keys always exist; if metadata is missing/older/unexpected this will raise and 500 the flow; should treat missing sender/login the same as a mismatch (invalid installation request)

get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) at line 434 is called without exception handling, and since the function calls resp.raise_for_status() which raises HTTPError on non-2xx responses, it causes an unhandled 500 error instead of the graceful error page used by other failure modes
Guard against missing sender metadata before dereference - if sender is absent (e.g., legacy integrations), this raises a KeyError and yields a 500; should treat it as invalid instead

The authenticated-user == installer check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet; build_integration then resolves any installation_id via the app JWT, so anyone knowing an installation id can claim it into their org until the installation webhook is processed

`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` can return `None` if the OAuth step was skipped or state was lost. Add an explicit `None` check before the comparison so the code fails clearly rather than relying on `None != <string>` semantics.

OAuthLoginView uses pipeline.signature as the OAuth state, but pipeline.signature is a deterministic MD5 of pipeline view class names, making the state guessable and not session-specific, which breaks OAuth CSRF/replay protection

Integration is fetched twice with inconsistent filters (first without status, second with status=ACTIVE): an extra query, and a non-active Integration without OrganizationIntegration now gets the generic error where it previously proceeded to next_step/ensure_integration
The `redirect_uri` should be URL-encoded before being included in the query string. Use `urllib.parse.quote()` to properly encode the URL.

The token exchange request at lines 427-431 is missing redirect_uri, but the authorize URL at line 408 explicitly includes it, violating RFC 6749 Section 4.1.3 which requires redirect_uri to be included in the token exchange request with an identical value if it was included in the authorization request
Test uses an invalid OAuth state, so the test never reaches the installation 404 path it is meant to cover.

OAuthLoginView hand-rolls an OAuth2 flow that already exists (OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView via NestedPipelineView + IdentityProviderPipeline); the copy lost the random state, urlencode and error logging

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

OAuthLoginView.dispatch() accepts installation_id from GET params unconditionally at lines 397-399, even during the OAuth callback phase, allowing an attacker to craft a callback URL containing their own installation_id, code, and the predictable state value to overwrite both sides of the sender comparison and bypass sender verification
error() calls _(error_short) on a variable while call sites now pass plain literals, so makemessages no longer extracts these strings and existing translations will drop on the next catalog rebuild
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value
The OAuth state used for CSRF protection is pipeline.signature, which is a constant computed from view class names that anyone can calculate, providing no actual CSRF protection

The OAuth `state` parameter is set to `pipeline.signature`, which is a deterministic MD5 hash of pipeline identifiers — not a per-request random value. OAuth 2.0 requires `state` to be an unpredictable, per-request nonce to prevent CSRF. Consider generating a cryptographically random token and storing it in the pipeline state for verification on callback.

Token-exchange/user-fetch failures are mishandled: safe_urlopen and get_user_info are outside the try block, so network errors or GitHub 4xx/5xx give a 500 instead of the error page; meanwhile the broad except Exception around safe_urlread/parse silently swallows errors with no logging

integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] at line 503 will raise a KeyError for any Integration whose metadata lacks a sender key, since the sender field is only conditionally added during build_integration
The setup_path + urlencode({code, state=<md5>}) block is copy-pasted six times with the magic state hash hardcoded each time in tests
Authorize URL built by f-string without URL-encoding client_id, state, redirect_uri

`integration.metadata["sender"]` raises `KeyError` when the integration was built without a `sender` in state (the key is set conditionally in `build_integration`). Use `.get()` with a safe default, e.g., `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`.
Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
The new user-match check reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard, causing KeyError and HTTP 500 on the reinstall path when an Integration exists without a 'sender' key in metadata
Identity check compares mutable GitHub login strings instead of stable user id; a user who renamed their account between install and link is wrongly rejected
Test uses mismatched state which triggers state check failure instead of exercising the installation-not-found 404 path as intended

integration.metadata['sender']['login'] raises KeyError (HTTP 500) when the Integration has no 'sender' metadata, which is the normal state for pipeline-created or pre-existing integrations on the reinstall path
The authorize URL at :404-408 is built with an f-string without URL-encoding redirect_uri, client_id and state parameters, which will break if any parameter contains &, ? or # characters
Broad exception catch when parsing OAuth token response can mask unexpected failures - catching Exception is too general, and parse_qsl() with default parameters won't raise ValueError as expected

OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a constant md5 of view class names identical for every user/session, so the state check provides no CSRF protection; an attacker can forge the setup callback into a victim's in-progress pipeline, binding the attacker's GitHub login

issues.claim: The user-match check reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without a guard. Integrations whose metadata lacks a 'sender' key (build_integration only adds it conditionally, and older or pre-existing integrations may not have it) raise a KeyError, which produces an HTTP 500.

The OAuth authorize redirect URL is built with an f-string or string interpolation and does not URL-encode client_id, state or redirect_uri. Parameters containing characters such as &, ? or # produce a malformed URL or unintended query parsing.

OAuthLoginView uses pipeline.signature as the OAuth state. This is a deterministic MD5 of pipeline view class names, identical for every user and session, so it is guessable. As a result the state check gives no CSRF protection, and an attacker can forge a setup callback that binds the attacker's GitHub login and installation into a victim's pipeline.

OAuthLoginView.dispatch() accepts installation_id from GET params unconditionally, including during the OAuth callback phase. A crafted callback URL with an attacker's installation_id, code and the predictable state can therefore overwrite both sides of the sender comparison.

safe_urlopen() and get_user_info() (which calls raise_for_status()) are outside exception handling. Network errors or non-2xx responses during the token exchange or user fetch cause an unhandled 500 instead of the error() page.
The token-response parsing is wrapped in a broad 'except Exception', which masks unexpected failures. Also, parse_qsl() with default parameters does not raise ValueError as expected.

test_installation_not_found sends an OAuth state that does not match the pipeline signature. OAuthLoginView rejects it at the state check before build_integration runs, so the 404 installation-not-found path is never exercised.

The authenticated-user vs installer check is skipped when no Integration row exists yet. build_integration then resolves any installation_id via the app JWT, so anyone who knows an installation id can claim it into their org before the installation webhook is processed.
pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") can return None if the OAuth step was skipped or the state was lost. The comparison has no explicit None check.

Integration is fetched twice with inconsistent filters: first without a status filter, then with status=ACTIVE. This adds a query, and a non-active Integration without an OrganizationIntegration now gets the generic error instead of proceeding to next_step/ensure_integration.
The token exchange request omits redirect_uri even though the authorize URL includes it. RFC 6749 Section 4.1.3 requires the same redirect_uri in the token request.

OAuthLoginView hand-rolls an OAuth2 flow that already exists as OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView via NestedPipelineView and IdentityProviderPipeline. The copy lost the random state, urlencode and error logging.

error() calls _(error_short) on a variable, while call sites pass plain literals. makemessages therefore no longer extracts these strings, and their translations will be dropped on the next catalog rebuild.
In the tests, the setup_path + urlencode({code, state=<md5>}) block is duplicated six times, with the magic state hash hardcoded each time.
The identity check compares GitHub login strings, which can change, rather than the stable user id. A user who renamed their account between install and link is wrongly rejected.
